description: Lets have a challange and play with whats going wrong.
summary:
Earth Trail Detective follows one pollutant through its life cycle. Such pollutants can be sulfur dioxide, soot, dust and so on. It turns curated NASA satellite and model variables *OMI, MODIS, AIRS, GPM, IMERG, MERRA/2, GLDAS(into monthly, de-seasonalised time series for one or two
regions and reports the rate of change, its statistical significance and a confidence
interval in plain language. A trail view shows air, cloud, precipitation, glacier,
soil and river side by side; where NASA has no data, a "trail goes cold" card explains
why. This answers the challenge directly: find the right variables, get a long series
for a region, quantify the change and test whether it is real – including opposite
trends of the same process in two regions, such as sulfur over eastern North America
and India. Students get a guided mode, researchers an expert form. Free, open source
and offline-ready for classrooms.
details: Earth Trail Detective lets anyone ask "Is this changing – and can we prove it?" about pollutants in the Earth system. Pick a substance (sulfur, soot, dust, smoke, nitrogen, microplastics), a region and a period. The app shows one trend card per step of the substance's path through the water cycle: air → cloud → precipitation/snow → glacier/snowpack → soil (water as carrier) → river/ocean. Each card states what was measured, where, how strong the change is per decade, and whether it is statistically significant – or "No evidence", shown just as prominently. Where NASA has no time series for a step, a "trail goes cold" card explains why.
